site.name: github-404
site.summary: github-404-clone Clone of the GitHub 404 error page. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | 404 page: top GitHub nav bar, centered error message ("This is not the web page you are looking for."), Octocat illustration, links to home / search / contact support | | `style.css` | Dark background, illustration styling, buttons | | `app.js` | Illustration hover / parallax effect, (optional) fake search suggestions |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full github-404 system, prioritizing the primary error page flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The GitHub 404 page offers helpful recovery paths (search, support, status) but suffers from pervasive mobile usability and accessibility issues. Critical tap targets across the header navigation, filter buttons, and search suggestions fall well below the 44px minimum, making touch interactions frustrating. Additionally, the logo link is a dead-end with no accessible label, and the support form lacks client-side validation, allowing empty submissions.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the GitHub 404 error page, focusing on interactive recovery paths, visual feedback, and mobile responsiveness.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will focus entirely on the single index.html page, validating the search input, category filters, and navigation links. It will assess the parallax effect on the Octocat illustration and verify the behavior of all interactive elements. Finally, it will repeat critical checks on a mobile viewport to evaluate the numerous small tap target warnings identified in the prescan.
assumptions: Links with href '#' are intentionally non-functional in this clone but should still be clicked to check for unexpected errors or missing feedback.
The app.js parallax effect is tied to mouse movement over the illustration area.
The search input and category buttons (Code, Repositories, People) may trigger fake search suggestions or UI changes handled by app.js.
risk_hotspots: Empty interactive label on the logo link (ux-1)
Small tap targets on footer links (contact support, GitHub Status) and category buttons (Code, Repositories, People)
Search input and button interaction flow (lack of form tag might affect expected behaviors)

phases.title: Header Navigation Validation
phases.objective: Validate the accessibility and behavior of the top navigation bar controls.
key_checks: Click the logo link (ux-1) and verify behavior, noting the empty accessible label
Click the 'Search', 'Support', and 'Status' nav links and check for any visual feedback or console errors
exit_criteria: All header links have been clicked
Accessibility issue with the logo link is documented

phases.title: Search and Recovery Flow
phases.objective: Test the primary user recovery flow via the search input and category filters.
key_checks: Type a query into the 'Search GitHub' input (ux-5) and observe if fake suggestions appear
Click the 'Search' button (ux-6) to submit the query and check for UI response
Click the 'Code', 'Repositories', and 'People' filter buttons (ux-7, ux-8, ux-9) and verify state changes or visual feedback
exit_criteria: Search input has been typed into and submitted
All three category filter buttons have been interacted with

phases.title: Illustration and Footer Interaction
phases.objective: Validate the visual parallax effect and footer link behaviors.
key_checks: Hover/move mouse over the Octocat illustration area to trigger the parallax effect
Click the 'contact support' link (ux-10) and check for feedback
Click the 'GitHub Status' link (ux-11) and check for feedback
exit_criteria: Parallax effect is confirmed working or not working
Footer links have been clicked and behaviors observed

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Checks
phases.objective: Evaluate layout shifts, tap target usability, and parallax behavior on a mobile viewport.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and check for layout overlapping or broken styling
Verify if small tap targets (especially footer links and category buttons) are usable or severely impacted
Test touch interactions on the illustration for the parallax effect
exit_criteria: Mobile layout has been screenshot and assessed
Tap target severity has been validated via interaction

coverage_targets.features: 100% of visible controls (11 interactables) and the parallax visual effect
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat all critical interactions and layout checks on mobile viewport

notes: Pay special attention to the lack of a <form> element around the search input and button, which might affect standard submit behaviors.
Document whether the small tap targets identified in the prescan actually hinder interaction on the mobile viewport.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the page on a mobile device
findings.problem: Header navigation links (Search, Support, Status) have tap target heights of only 25px, severely violating the 44px mobile touch target guidance.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flag Search (62x25px), Support (68x25px), and Status (57x25px) links as small tap targets across multiple mobile trajectory steps (e.g., steps-31-36, steps-43-48).
findings.why_it_matters: Users with motor impairments or those on touch devices will struggle to accurately tap these links, leading to mis-taps and frustration.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding or height of the header navigation links to ensure a minimum tap target size of 44x44px on mobile viewports.
findings.source_hint: index.html: header nav links (ux-2, ux-3, ux-4)

findings.user_goal: Understand the purpose of the logo link and navigate home
findings.problem: The GitHub logo link has an empty accessible label (name: '#') and acts as a dead link (href='#'), providing no context for screen reader users and no functional navigation.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag the logo link (ux-1) as an 'empty_interactive_label'. Clicking it resulted in 'no visible page change or navigation', confirming it is a placeholder.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will hear an empty or meaningless label, failing to convey the link's purpose. Sighted users expecting to return to the homepage by clicking the logo will be confused when nothing happens.
findings.suggestion: Add an aria-label (e.g., 'GitHub Homepage') to the logo link and update the href to the actual homepage URL instead of '#'.

findings.user_goal: Submit a support request for the 404 error
findings.problem: The 'Contact Support' form allows submission without filling out the required fields (Email, Subject, Description), lacking client-side validation.
findings.evidence: In steps-25-30, clicking the 'Submit Request' button successfully changed its text to 'Submitted' without filling out any form fields, indicating empty support requests can be processed.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may accidentally submit incomplete forms, leading to frustration when support doesn't respond, and creating invalid data on the backend.
findings.suggestion: Implement client-side validation to prevent form submission and display inline error messages when required fields are left empty.

findings.user_goal: Refine search queries using suggestion links
findings.problem: Search suggestion links (e.g., 'react', 'python', 'node') have severely undersized tap targets (31x16px), making them incredibly difficult to hit on touch screens.
findings.evidence: In step agentic-49-click, the 'react' suggestion link (ux-43) was measured at 31x16px, far below the 44px mobile guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Users will likely mis-tap these small links, hitting adjacent elements or having to make multiple attempts, causing significant friction in the search recovery flow.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding around suggestion links to expand their tap area to at least 44x44px.

findings.user_goal: Search for a repository or code snippet
findings.problem: When the search panel is revealed, focus is not automatically moved to the search input, forcing users to manually locate and click into the field.
findings.evidence: In steps-01-06, it was noted that 'the transition relies entirely on visual feedback without focus management (focus was not automatically moved to the input)'.
findings.why_it_matters: Auto-focusing the input saves users an extra click and clearly indicates where they should start typing, especially important for keyboard and screen reader users.
findings.suggestion: Programmatically set focus to the search input element when the search panel is toggled open.

findings.user_goal: Subscribe to status updates via email
findings.problem: The email subscription input lacks an explicit accessible label, relying solely on the placeholder 'you@example.com', which disappears upon typing.
findings.evidence: In steps-13-18, it was observed that 'The email input lacks an explicit accessible label, relying solely on the placeholder... which disappears upon typing and negatively impacts screen reader accessibility.'
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users may not know what the field is for if it lacks a proper label, and sighted users lose context once they start typing if the placeholder vanishes.
findings.suggestion: Add a visible label element associated with the input, or use an aria-label attribute to provide an accessible name.

findings.user_goal: Expand FAQ questions for more information
findings.problem: FAQ accordion buttons lack a visible toggle indicator (like a chevron or +/- icon), reducing discoverability that they are expandable.
findings.evidence: In steps-07-12, it was noted that 'The FAQ accordion buttons lack a visible toggle indicator... which could reduce discoverability that they are expandable.'
findings.why_it_matters: Without visual cues, users may not realize they can click the questions to reveal answers, missing out on helpful self-service information.
findings.suggestion: Add a chevron or plus/minus icon to the accordion buttons that rotates or changes state upon expansion to signal interactivity.

findings.user_goal: Filter search results on a mobile device
findings.problem: Search filter buttons (Code, Repositories, People) have tap target heights of 38px, falling below the 44px mobile touch target guidance.
findings.evidence: In steps-43-48, layout warnings flagged the filter buttons (Code 65x38px, Repositories 110x38px, People 76x38px) as small tap targets.
findings.why_it_matters: While slightly better than the header links, these undersized targets still pose a minor usability challenge for touch interaction, increasing the risk of mis-taps.
findings.suggestion: Increase the vertical padding of the filter buttons to reach a minimum height of 44px.

gaps: 48% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
